title: From age 17 to Chainsaw Man
lede: Shikaku was not born in a vacuum. Scroll sideways to see where it sits in Tatsuki Fujimoto's career.
hint: Keep scrolling: the timeline moves sideways.
intro: Tatsuki Fujimoto drew short stories from his teens. The 17-21 and 22-26 collections are titled after his age when he drew them, so reading them feels like opening a creative diary.
The years below are release or creation years listed in official sources and public references. We deliberately give years only, not exact dates, to avoid unverified detail.

events.title: A Couple Clucking Chickens Were Still Kickin' in the Schoolyard
Sasaki Stopped a Bullet
events.body: A one-shot about a teacher named Sasaki and his student.

events.title: Love is Blind
events.body: A school romance with a confession that keeps getting delayed.

events.title: Shikaku
events.body: Assassin vs immortal vampire. The closing story of 17-21, and the reason this site exists.

events.title: Nayuta of the Prophecy
events.body: A little sister with the power to end the world.

events.title: Fire Punch
events.body: His first long series (Shōnen Jump+). A body that keeps burning and keeps healing.

events.title: Chainsaw Man
events.body: Began in Weekly Shōnen Jump. Part two continued on Shōnen Jump+.

events.title: Look Back
events.body: A long one-shot about two girls who draw manga. Adapted into a film in 2024.

events.title: The 17-21 & 22-26 collections
events.body: Shueisha collected eight early short stories. VIZ's English editions followed in 2023.

events.title: Goodbye, Eri
events.body: A one-shot about film, memory, and beautiful lies.

events.title: Tatsuki Fujimoto 17-26 anime
events.body: Eight short stories adapted; Shikaku is episode 4.

dnaLede: Threads fans find in nearly all his work, already clearly visible in Shikaku.

dna.title: Violence as a joke
dna.body: A shattered body is treated like a sight gag, which makes sincere emotion land as a shock.
dna.inShikaku: Yugeru complains about his clothes, not his wounds.

dna.title: The stabbing pause
dna.body: Empty, silent panels right after chaos. Fujimoto is often called deeply cinematic in how he times a pause.
dna.inShikaku: The silent castle after Shikaku leaves.

dna.title: The uncontrollable character
dna.body: Characters who are dangerous, childish, and sincere at once. Violence is their language for getting close.
dna.inShikaku: Shikaku's love, born from a target she failed to kill.

dna.title: Bodies that refuse to die
dna.body: Regeneration returns again and again, from comedy to tragedy.

dna.title: Love of film and screens
dna.body: Cinema references and screens often become a key part of the story.
dna.inShikaku: A climax that happens on live television.

dna.title: Endings that turn tender
dna.body: After all the madness, his stories often close on something warm and strange.
dna.inShikaku: An invitation to stay for thousands of years.
